# Security policy

## Supported version

Only the current `main` branch receives security fixes. Experimental branches,
historical documents, and old revisions are unsupported.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not disclose a suspected vulnerability in an issue, pull request, discussion,
or other public channel.

Once the repository is public, use GitHub's **Report a vulnerability** action to
open a private vulnerability report. Enabling private vulnerability reporting is
a mandatory publication gate in [the rollout plan](publication/README.md).

Before that gate is enabled, do not publish vulnerability details. Contact the
repository owner through their GitHub profile only to request a private reporting
channel; do not include technical details in the initial message.

Include affected revisions, impact, reproduction steps, and any known mitigation.
The owner will acknowledge receipt and coordinate disclosure after a fix is
available. No response-time or bounty commitment is made.
